item: the erase destroys the salt copies the write-ahead log and the rollback journal hold (R708)
summary: BEFORE: step 1 of quick_crypto_erase overwrote only the first 4 KiB of each encrypted database AND of its -wal and -journal. SQLCipher keeps the 16-byte salt in plaintext at the start of page 1, and every commit that touches page 1 leaves a copy of that page in a WAL frame (or the journal) far past those 4 KiB. Measured on a 20-commit WAL with checkpoints off: the salt sat in 21 places in the -wal, 20 of them beyond the head, so the erase left it readable. The uninstall watcher's embedded copy had the same gap. NOW: three passes: the -shm and main heads first (no unlink), then the -wal and -journal overwritten whole (one sequential write of the WAL's size, waiting on nothing), then the main and -shm heads again and unlinked, so a checkpoint during pass 2 cannot carry the salt home. The panic wipe also keeps a descriptor on each unlinked main, -wal and -journal (POSIX) and rewrites them after the pool is closed and once more 15 s later: the security read measured a transaction under way at the erase committing page 1, salt included, back into the unlinked file (rollback and WAL mode); a commit later than the last pass is the window left, stated in SECURITY.md. Then, after the keys, the cache and the anchors and before the slow step 6, every other regular file under the data dir has its head destroyed (step 4b: a -wal or -journal whole, a -shm zeroed): retained pre-restore snapshots and salvage copies carry the corpus salt in their first page and were reached only by step 6's full overwrite, so an erase stopped before it left them readable (verified; a test stops the erase there and finds no salt under the data dir). Not covered, stated: plaintext staging (backup members, an extracted restore, a reassembling archive) has no salt and an encrypted archive member sits past its head, both left to step 6. A folder that cannot be listed is now named in overwrite_failures (both walks were silent). 2,000 files add about 1.7 s, after the keys. The report gains other_heads_destroyed. No step writes through a link: every overwrite opens with O_NOFOLLOW (where the platform has it) and writes only a regular file, so a symlinked sidecar, key file, anchors.db or any other name is removed and never written through, and a FIFO, socket or device is never opened to write; a symlinked folder or a Windows junction is never entered. The app's own databases are the one exception: one linked into place is erased where it really is. Measured on the old code: step 6 overwrote a file OUTSIDE the data dir through a symlink and hung on a FIFO, and steps 1, 2 and 4 wrote through linked sidecars, keys and anchors. Still true and stated: a hard-linked file shares its bytes with its other names, and a mount point under the data dir is walked like any folder. No broad-location guard exists for an explicit OO_DATA_DIR (home, drive root); step 1b has exactly step 6's scope, which already overwrote and removed everything there. Tests read the WAL and journal back through a hard link outside the data dir after the erase and find no salt (real SQLCipher WAL with the connection still open; synthetic journal; the watcher); all three fail on the old code; a fourth reproduces the late commit in both journal modes and proves the rewrite. SECURITY.md now says step 6 overwrites every remaining file whole, so a future large file under the data dir needs its own unlink-only step after its key is gone. Release line: The emergency wipe now also destroys the copies of the database's key salt kept in its write-ahead log and journal, including what a write still in progress puts back, and the salt of every encrypted snapshot of the corpus before anything slower.
